title: unified-rollouts: weighted canary + shadow auto-rollback workflow
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customers want safer progressive rollouts when using combined weighted canary + shadow traffic strategies. The current unified-rollouts engine supported simple canary and shadow modes independently but lacked a first-class workflow for mixed weighted canaries that also run shadow probing traffic and trigger automated rollback based on composite metric quorums and quarantine rules.

This PR implements: 1) a weighted canary scheduler that can split live traffic across multiple model variants with per-stage weight ramps; 2) a shadow probing overlay that sends sampled traffic to shadow variants and aggregates probe metrics into the rollout decision loop; 3) an autorollback engine extension that evaluates composite metric quorums (latency + error-rate + quality regression) with configurable thresholds and a quarantine stage before full rollback; 4) observability hooks and tracing spans for per-variant metrics, probe-sample IDs, and decision traces; 5) rollout API additions for specifying weighted-stages, shadow-probing-config, and quarantine windows; 6) e2e tests and stability guards to avoid flapping on short-lived signal spikes.

Checklist: - [x] Weighted scheduler algorithm + deterministic traffic split tests - [x] Shadow probing sampler + probe metrics pipeline - [x] Composite metric quorum evaluator + quarantine stage - [x] API schema updates (rollout v2) + backwards compatibility checks - [x] Observability dashboards and alerts updates - [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Docs and migration notes

Compatibility and migration notes: rollout v2 expands the rollout spec with optional weightedStages and shadowProbe fields; existing rollouts without weightedStages continue to behave as before. Customers with pinned model variants are unaffected. Admins can opt into rollout v2 via a feature flag on the Console; rollout controller handles mixed-version clusters during rollout.

Risk and mitigations: the primary risk is oscillation when noisy probe metrics trigger repeated quarantines. Mitigations include: configurable quorum size, minimum stable window, and cooldown windows between successive quarantines. We added stability guards and integration tests that simulate flapping.

References: ENG-4321 (design RFC), ENG-4399 (observability follow-up), related PRs for rollback observability and safety guards.

review_comments: Eric Patel (2026-02-14): Overall looks solid. Two concerns: (1) can we expose quorum size as a percentage rather than absolute counts? (2) the scheduler's deterministic hashing needs clear doc explaining key selection to avoid cross-tenant collisions.

Maya Chen (2026-02-14): Answered: we expose quorum both as percent and absolute; added examples in migration doc. Scheduler uses request fingerprint (tenant + route + user_id when present) — added doc and tests.
Sofia Ramirez (2026-02-18): Observability LGTM but please add a low-cardinality probe_id tag for metrics to make aggregation cheaper. Also add an alert for repeated quarantines within a 10m window.
Maya Chen (2026-02-18): Added probe_id tag and an alert rule. Also added a cooldown param and test coverage for repeated quarantines.
Liam O'Connor (2026-02-25): Integration tests flaky on CI (we saw a timeout in e2e). Suggest increasing default timeouts for the simulated probe backend and add retry on transient errors.
Maya Chen (2026-02-26): Increased timeouts and added retry logic with exponential backoff in the e2e harness; re-ran CI and validated stability.
